Dataset.Name: SchwingNet corpus: real C-arm exposures with volumetric truth, rendered CT, level-annotated radiographs and the transitional-person inventory (state of 2026-09-24)
Dataset.Summary: The data behind the SchwingNet manuscript (five figures, three tables; 2026-09-24). Assembled from public releases only; nothing was acquired and the derived layout is not redistributed because the source licences differ. Table 1 of the manuscript (SchwingNet/tables/tab_corpus.md, every cell traced in tab_corpus.sources.md) counts 4,093 renders of labelled CT (CTSpinoPelvic1K 801, TotalSegmentator v2 1,170 and v3 1,735, VerSe 387), 9,108 level-annotated films (CSXA 4,963, BUU-LSPINE 3,603 lateral, NHANES II 542) and 4,276 real exposures with three-dimensional truth (C-ArmLSpine 296, DeepFluoro 366, COBRA2026 Elekta 3,480, Geneva 116, Ljubljana 18), of which 778 come from mobile C-arms. The intraoperative test set is C-ArmLSpine: 148 lumbar cases on one C-arm, cone-beam CT truth from two automatic labellers agreeing on 814 of 910 vertebrae. Transitional persons, typed from each source's own truth under a rib convention (tables/tab4_transitional.md): 194 in all, 110 with L6, 7 with T13, 28 with a sacralised L5 (12 with four lumbar vertebrae), 31 Castellvi I/II, 14 with a lumbar rib, 4 unassigned; the only real intraoperative ones are three C-ArmLSpine L6 of one automatic labeller, and a COBRA2026 screen adds 38 L6 and 45 T13 calls that no person has read. The built person-disjoint split (50/10/40 within subtype) puts 43 L6 and 3 T13 CT persons and the three real L6 on the test side. Known defects are under Noise; aliases that make one person several names are under Relationships between instances.

Descriptors.Comments: Assembler of the derived layout, not the originator of any image; the originating releases are under References. No ORCID iD is recorded in the repository. Card updated 2026-09-23 for the six-figure manuscript and 2026-09-24 (SchwingNet/atlas/README.md, 'What changed').
Descriptors.Contact: Gregory J. Schwing, MD, PhD, Department of General Surgery, Wayne State University School of Medicine / Detroit Medical Center; [e-mail withheld]
Descriptors.Ethical review: No new patient data were acquired. The Wayne State University IRB Administration Office issued a Notice of IRB Administrative Determination on 2026-09-02 (WSU IRB HPR Number 2026-269, 'Open Spine Consortium: Secondary Analysis of Publicly Available, De-Identified Imaging Datasets and the Derived Annotations, Software, and Models Produced From Them'): not human participant research under 45 CFR 46 or FDA regulations; IRB review not required (the signed notice was read page by page on 2026-09-23). The determination covers sources that are public, de-identified before release and downloadable without application or data use agreement. VinDr-SpineXR, whose films sit in the intraoperative fold banks, is released by PhysioNet only under its Restricted Health Data Use Agreement and is outside that scope; a separate determination, or retraining without it, is open before submission. One C-ArmLSpine directory (case134/ori, 302 XA frames) carries a real PatientID and name; it is excluded from every bank and never printed.
Descriptors.Funding: None declared (the author confirms on the full title page). Compute: Wayne State University High Performance Computing Grid.

Descriptors.Version: State of 2026-09-24. Manifest with SHA-256 over each input file list: docs/RSNAI_DATA_MANIFEST.json (2026-09-22). Transitional inventory: SchwingNet/results/rare_class/transitional_subtypes.csv and split_plan.md (2026-09-23), as the manuscript's Table 2 prints it; the overnight screens of 2026-09-24 (VerSe, all 355 people; TotalSegmentator v3, 1,935 scans; docs/RESUME_2026-09-22_PM.md) will change those counts when Table 2 is regenerated, and this card follows the table. COBRA2026 is complete on disk (692 of 692 cases) but the reported banks hold the 145 Elekta cases fetched before the analysis.

Dataset properties.Confidentiality: All sources are public and de-identified at source; this project adds no identifiers and receives no re-identification key. One exception is recorded: the C-ArmLSpine release directory case134/ori holds 302 XA frames without a .dcm extension that carry a real PatientID and a real name; a *.dcm walk misses them. They are excluded from every bank and are never printed, and the identity specification (docs/PATIENT_IDENTITY_SPEC.md, alias 16) says so. DeepFluoro vendor DICOMs carry a PatientID that is the autopsy accession of a cadaver, not a living person.
Dataset properties.External data: Every image is external. Nothing was acquired, annotated by a clinician, or purchased. Derived by this project: the registered poses for C-ArmLSpine (tools/carmlspine_pose.py, 913 files), the projected boxes and level names, the fitted device cards, the styled synthetic renders, and the crop banks.
Dataset properties.Missing information: C-ArmLSpine: no PatientAge, PatientSex, PatientID or PatientBirthDate on any DICOM (checked in carmlspine/tags_case1.txt); whether 149 cases are 149 people is unknowable on disk. COBRA Elekta (145 cases): PatientAge present on 115 (26-92 years, median 66) and PatientSex on 75 (41 F, 34 M) of the per-case metadata.yaml files; centres D, F and G strip every identity remnant. DeepFluoro: six cadavers by accession, no age or sex. Geneva: one phantom. TotalSegmentator: no patient, accession or study field in either release; age is jittered by the release (992 of 1,228 shared ids differ between v2.0.1 and v3.0.0 by up to 4 years) and institute letters were remapped; one clean subject has no age and one no sex recorded. FluoroCap: patient_identifier_present = no on all 1,616 matched rows; a patient count cannot be given. AASCE: whether a film index is one person is not established. COBRA Varian: pitch, kVp and device fields not recorded in the headers read so far. SpineSAC: no bone truth built; not in any bank. CTSpinoPelvic1K CT 0533: published truncated in the Hugging Face mirror (the Zenodo record carries no CT); the mirror copy was replaced with the rebuild on 2026-09-23 (sha256 478a74e9...), after the render banks were built, so the banks still hold 801 of 802. Indication, habitus and instrumentation are not recorded for any intraoperative case.
Dataset properties.Motivation: To ask whether a vertebral level can be named from operating-room C-arm exposures alone, with no preoperative 3-D scan, no registration and no tracked instrument. That needs real intraoperative fluoroscopy with 3-D truth (C-ArmLSpine), several different C-arms with paired frames and CT so each device's image formation can be fitted rather than assumed (DeepFluoro, COBRA, Geneva, Ljubljana), and enough labelled vertebrae to teach a network what a level looks like rather than how to count to it (the level bank). Assembled by Gregory Schwing on the Wayne State grid; the author has a commercial interest in a level-confirmation product under development.
Dataset properties.Noise: Known defects, each with the file that records it. (1) ~/verse_drr holds 387 files for 374 spines: 13 exact duplicate renders, glgl003...glgl146 repeating gl003...gl146 with identical shape and boxes (doubled-prefix naming bug); ~/verse_drr/path additionally holds 344 glverse* byte-identical duplicates (docs/ANOMALY_RULE_EVALUATION.md; docs/PATIENT_IDENTITY_SPEC.md alias 9). (2) verse_drr millimetres are suspected about 15 % short: measured mean lumbar centre-to-centre pitch 31.7 mm on verse108 against a published 36-38 mm, the known cause being the DRR row-spacing defect (A-P spacing written into the S-I row field, found 2026-09-19); ~/verse_drr/ann is dated 2026-09-19 12:57 and straddles the fix; no millimetre from verse_drr is quotable until one case is re-rendered post-sweep_v3 (docs/RESUME_2026-09-22_PM.md item A8). (3) CTSP_COLONOG_730 is named T10, T11, T12, L1, L2, L4, L5 with an ordinary centre-to-centre step (0.91 of its neighbours) between the bodies named L2 and L4: either four lumbar bodies named as five or L3 skipped; unresolved (item C7). (4) Level truth on C-ArmLSpine is two automatic labellers agreeing on 814 of 910 CBCT vertebrae (89.5 %; 41 name disagreements, 55 unmatched, 3 SPINEPS missing, 22 variant-flagged cases); the agreement filter names T11 in 0 of 3 boxes and T12 in 6 of 63, so the thoracolumbar junction is withheld from scoring; no level was established by a human (carmlspine/levels.json summary; realxray/carmlspine/summary.json). (5) C-ArmLSpine poses are registered, not supplied: median edge NCC 0.370 AP and 0.207 lateral; detector-vs-truth box offset median 0.01 body heights, one lateral frame beyond 0.25 (or_ready/audit/AUDIT.md (g)). (6) C-ArmLSpine ships a per-slice series UID and a placeholder PixelSpacing of 1.0; the real pitch is 307.2 mm / 2048. (7) 160 of 366 DeepFluoro frames are stored upside down (rot-180-for-up set on 160 frames, all 24 of specimen 17-1905); the fluoro PatientID splits and merges cadavers wrongly and is never used for identity. (8) COBRA Elekta has 74,364 cross-case near-duplicate pairs between train+val and test at NCC32 >= 0.97 (different patients at the same gantry angle, 0 same-case pairs); COBRA sacrum recall is partly a positional prior and should be read per angle bin. COBRA case B000 has 41 frames the CT never covers and is dropped. (9) The synthetic device corpus was drawn with device_style.SPREAD = 0.2 clipping every per-frame term to its central 60 %: a styled frame reaches 1.7-5.1 % of its device's fitted joint distribution and 94.9-98.3 % of styled frames carry at least one pinned term (docs/DEVICE_SPREAD_SWEEP.md); the typicality sampler exists but is not the default. (10) The encoder initialisation bank family (allspine_v2, v6, v7) carries two split leaks: NHANES II entered twice under independent splits (48 of 54 validation patients had their other copy in training) and CTSpinoPelvic1K under two naming schemes (357 people on both sides, measured on v6/v7; v2 was built the same way and was not separately measured); the v8 rebuild keyed VerSe series as subjects and leaks five patients (10.5 % of VerSe validation). (11) The VINDRPS crops in the fold banks come from vindrps_fov96_ctx, keyed per image rather than per study, whose own validation split leaks 77.8 %; they are pseudo-labels (VinDr releases lesion boxes, not levels). (12) FluoroCap: 72.8 % of literature panels have zero pixel residual against another panel (republished figures), so the identity is the image, not a patient; train only. (13) anchor_drr (not in these banks, but the corpus behind the render-only detector's own-domain figure) seeds its split on the implant-variant stem, putting 301 of 801 CTSpinoPelvic1K people on both sides. (14) TotalSegmentator v2.0.1 -> v3.0.0 is a renumber: 24 v2 ids are byte-identical to 24 different v3 ids and the vacated numbers were reissued to other people; keying on s#### alone splits 24 people and merges 15. Within v3, s1445 = s1446 and s2107 = s2109 = s2110 are byte-duplicates. (15) BUU-LSPINE 0140/0719 and 0449/0629 have byte-identical films. (16) CTSpinoPelvic1K CT 0533 was a truncated file in the public mirror (16.5 MiB, gzip EOFError); the mirror was repaired on 2026-09-23 (commit 72cd777) and the render bank still holds 801 of 802. (17) Transitional subtype calls from SPINEPS with VERIDAH (COBRA2026, C-ArmLSpine) are read by no person; on CTSpinoPelvic1K that labeller's L6 call matched the readers in 10 of 24 (tables/tab4_transitional.md note e). Twelve TotalSegmentator spines once called L6 from raw mask identifiers: eight read normal on an independent rib count (scrambled SPINEPS instance ids).
Dataset properties.Partitioning scheme: Real frame sets: split by case with int(md5(case), 16) % 10 -> 0-6 train, 7 val, 8-9 test; DeepFluoro fixed by specimen (train 17-1882, 17-1905, 18-2799, 18-2800; val 18-0725; test 18-1109); Geneva test only. Audited 2026-09-22: 0 cases in more than one split, 0 meta/splits.json disagreements, 0 images in the wrong split directory, 0 same-case near-duplicate pairs across splits (or_ready/audit/AUDIT.md (a), (b)). Level encoder and head: five-fold CV over C-ArmLSpine with md5(case) % 5 = k as the test fold; per fold the DRR bank, the context-crop bank and the mixed bank hold 0 crops of that fold's test cases and 0 split-rule violations. The detector of the model card (rx_lodo_carmlspine_1024) trains on COBRA Elekta train+val and DeepFluoro train+val, selects its checkpoint on COBRA test and DeepFluoro test, and is scored on the C-ArmLSpine test split, which it never saw under any name; only its held-out-device numbers are clean. Synthetic device corpus: the same 17 TotalSegmentator validation subjects in every styled corpus (STYLE_INFO.json), so a subject is on one side under every geometry and noise card; the pooled list builder refuses to write if a CT subject or a real specimen falls on two sides. Caveat that must travel with the CV number: it is split by case, and whether the 148 C-ArmLSpine cases are 148 people cannot be established (PatientID empty on 59,307 of 59,609 instances; 149 cases fall on five acquisition dates at a median 224 s apart); the fallback with folds grouped by acquisition day was run and reads 92.54 % [87.7, 96.4] lateral whole frame against 98.22 % case-grouped (SchwingNet/results/a9.json).
Dataset properties.Re-identification: No attempt is made and no key exists. One real identifier is known to be present in a source and is excluded: C-ArmLSpine case134/ori, 302 XA frames without a .dcm extension carrying a real PatientID and a real PatientName, neither of which is reproduced here. Those frames are in no bank, no figure and no log, and the name is not reproduced here or anywhere in the repository's documents beyond the identity specification that records the exclusion. The private tag (0029,0016) used to key C-ArmLSpine acquisitions is an un-stripped console identifier that keys an acquisition, not a person, and is used only for split integrity. Every other corpus is keyed by a release id, a specimen accession, a study UID or a document id per docs/PATIENT_IDENTITY_SPEC.md, and content hashes are used only to merge, never to identify.
Dataset properties.Relationships between instances: One person can appear under several names, and the identity specification (docs/PATIENT_IDENTITY_SPEC.md section 3) lists nineteen aliases that must collapse to one key. The ones touching this corpus: (a) C-ArmLSpine case<N> (realxray meta/splits) = case<N>_AP / case<N>_LAT (carm_drr ann) = the same people restated in carm_cv0..cv4_drr under different split labels; the CV banks and carm_drr are never pooled. (b) BUU-LSPINE: films_drr / films_drr_buucorr (3,603 lateral) and films_ap_drr (3,600 AP) carry the same 3,600 patients; AP and lateral are two items of one person, and MEND_<NNNN> in mendeley_drr redistributes 500 of them. (c) NHANES II: NHANES_nhanes_(cervical|lumbar)_<id> (films_drr) = NH_<id>_c/l (nhanes_drr) = NHANESPS_[CL]<id> (nhanes_pseudo); cervical and lumbar films of one sample person share the 5-digit id; both films_drr and nhanes_drr copies sit in the fold banks. (d) CTSpinoPelvic1K: CTSP_COLONOG_<token>[_s<k>] (ctsp_drr) = ctsp_<release>_(ap|lat)[_p<k>][_s<j>] (physics_drr, anchor_drr) = implant_<release>_v<k>_<view> (implant renders are the same person as the clean render); token is not the release id (release 0145 = token 100) and 34 of 802 tokens are CTC-<10 digits>. (e) VerSe: 374 series belong to 355 subjects (verse400-417 own 37 series); gl003 = glgl003 (duplicate render) = gl003_p0 (verse_drr_obl) = gl003_s0 (verse_drr_film) = CTSP_VERSE_gl003_p0 (ctsp_drr_obl, which holds VerSe series under a CTSP prefix). (f) TotalSegmentator: TS_s#### (ts_drr) = totalseg_s####_(ap|lat)[_p<k>][_s<j>] (anchor_drr, physics_drr) = s####_<k>_<pose>.npz (devcorpus), after the 24-row v2->v3 renumber table and the three intra-v3 byte-duplicate groups; the 17 devcorpus validation subjects also appear in up to five CT render banks. (g) VinDr: VINDR_vindr_<image_id> = VINDRPS_<image_id> = MEND_<image_id>, and an image id belongs to a study id (10,466 images -> 5,000 studies). (h) DeepFluoro: H5 group /17-1882 = directory ..._cadaver_17-1882 = ipcai_2020_ds_8x specimen 01 (crosswalk 01=17-1882, 02=18-1109, 03=18-0725, 04=18-2799, 05=18-2800, 06=17-1905); the registered frames and the vendor DICOMs are one dataset in two representations and are never counted twice. (i) FluoroCap: panels __a and __b of one figure are one patient; one article can appear under pmc:, art:s2_<sha1>, art:W<n>, doi: and url: route ids; video panels key to the video id. (j) Whole-bank subsets: fluorocap_drr_smoke is a subset of fluorocap_drr; films_drr_buucorr has the same 9,109 case names as films_drr; the four cobra_elekta* banks share 145 case ids.
Dataset properties.Sampling: Subsets cut by download volume, with no criterion. COBRA2026: 152 Elekta and 26 Varian cases fetched before the analysis of 692 public (six centres, A-D Elekta and F-G Varian); 145 Elekta cases in splits; the full release is now on disk (692 of 692) and not yet in any bank. C-ArmLSpine: 148 of 149 released cases built. TotalSegmentator: a clean whole-spine subject list of 142 (100 polytrauma studies), not the whole release. DeepFluoro: all 366 registered frames. Geneva: all 116 frames. Level bank per fold: fixed-scale context crops drawn from each source bank as listed under the Training partition; the film sources are subsets of larger corpora chosen by the availability of per-vertebra labels (CSXA 4,963 films of 4,963; BUU 3,603 of 7,204; NHANES 543 of 17,073 with landmarks). Synthetic device corpus: each of the 142 subjects rendered under each device's real pose pool and styled through each device card (P_pooled list: 12,730 synthetic training entries, 1,998 validation entries). Sampling of the per-frame physics terms is clipped to the central 60 % of each marginal (a measured defect; see Noise 9).
Dataset properties.Sensitive data: None beyond the excluded case134/ori frames (see Re-identification). Cadaveric specimens (DeepFluoro, Ljubljana) are identified by accession only. No clinical indication, diagnosis or outcome is present for any intraoperative case.

Procedures.Name: Intraoperative lumbar spine C-arm fluoroscopy, AP and lateral (C-ArmLSpine)
Pelvic kV cone-beam CT projection sweeps for radiotherapy setup (COBRA2026 Elekta XVI)
Cadaveric pelvic C-arm fluoroscopy with registered CT (DeepFluoro)
Phantom hip C-arm fluoroscopy with gold-standard poses (Geneva)
Whole-spine CT (TotalSegmentator, VerSe, CTSpinoPelvic1K) rendered as digitally reconstructed radiographs
Plain lateral and AP spine radiography (CSXA, BUU-LSPINE, NHANES II)

Imaging.Resolution: Real frames are exported to 8-bit 1024 x 1024 PNG. Native: C-ArmLSpine 2048 x 2048 at 0.15 mm (object-plane 0.1915 mm at 1024 export; SID 1140 mm, SOD 745 mm), kVp 73-111; COBRA Elekta XVI 504 x 504 at 0.8 mm, 120 kVp; DeepFluoro Cios Fusion 1536 x 1536 at 0.194 mm, kVp not in the registered frames (it is in the vendor DICOM headers of the same acquisitions, docs/DEVICE_PARAM_AUDIT.md, not joined per frame); Geneva BV Pulsera 1000 x 1000 at 0.2904 mm, 62-110 kV full range per docs/devices/bv_pulsera.json (65-90 kVp at the 5th-95th percentile in docs/RSNAI_TABLE1_DATASETS.md); Ljubljana PIXIUM 4600 1560 x 1560 at 0.286 mm. Level-bank crops: 2 x 320 x 320 fixed-scale context windows with the target body at 96 px. Device cards are fitted at a coarse pitch (0.776-0.858 mm, 372-520 px).
Imaging.Pre-processing: Stored value -> attenuation per device (log display, linear, neg-log or neg-log-offset, recorded per frame as stored_value / conversion); one display window for every device (field percentiles 1/5/50/95/99 mapped onto 27/47/126/216/239, the FluoroCap operating-room medians), bone bright; boxes by projecting every mask voxel (<= 20k points) through K.ext, 2nd-98th percentile extent, kept when visible_frac >= 0.5 and both sides >= 8 px; two labellers, agreed levels only, null-level boxes kept for detection and excluded from naming; splits by case as above; contact sheets under qc/ per dataset are looked at before any number is reported (docs/REAL_XRAY_DATASETS_SPEC.md). Synthetic frames: whole-spine CT ray-cast under real device poses, styled through the nine fitted terms (tools/device_style.py) with photons fitted and drawn before receptor blur; CT volumes are canonicalised to analyse and never reoriented when written.
Imaging.Comments: Burned-in PHI was not audited frame by frame. What is known: FluoroCap records patient_identifier_present = no on all 1,616 matched rows; C-ArmLSpine and DeepFluoro exports are pixel data only, but the C-ArmLSpine case134/ori XA frames are excluded because their headers carry a name. RadLex RIDs for fluoroscopy, CT and radiography were recalled from memory and not verified against the RadLex server; cone-beam CT is given by name only (VALIDATION.md). 'Other' covers HDF5 (DeepFluoro registered frames), MHA and YAML (COBRA), NPZ (Geneva, devcorpus renders) and JPEG/TIFF plain films.

Total.Criterion: Real frames of the two training devices for the model card's detector (rx_lodo_carmlspine_1024): COBRA Elekta train + val and DeepFluoro train + val, per the by-case md5 split and the by-specimen DeepFluoro split.
Total.Comments: One exam = one exported frame with its projected boxes. Patient count is not additive: 118 COBRA Elekta cases (the dataset paper's authority that one case is one patient) plus five cadaveric specimens.

Total.Sex: 41 F / 34 M on the 75 of 145 Elekta cases whose metadata carries PatientSex; unknown on the rest
Total.Demographic: Living pelvic radiotherapy patients at four European centres (A-D); age known on 115 of 145 cases (median 66 years).
Total.Criterion: COBRA2026 Elekta XVI cases with a registered planning CT; md5(case) % 10 in 0-7 (train 110 cases / 2,640 frames, val 8 cases / 192 frames); case B000 dropped (41 frames outside the CT).
Total.Comments: Age and sex figures are computed over all 145 Elekta cases in the splits, not the 118 training cases alone. 22,260 cross-case near-duplicate frame pairs exist between train and val (same gantry angle, different patients).

Total.Demographic: Cadaveric pelves (Johns Hopkins autopsy accessions 17-1882, 17-1905, 18-2799, 18-2800 train; 18-0725 val); no age or sex recorded.
Total.Criterion: DeepFluoro registered frames, fixed split by specimen (train 238 frames, val 24).
Total.Comments: The registered pipeline keys by specimen; the fluoro-DICOM PatientID is wrong and unused.

Partitions.Comments: The detector's checkpoint was selected on COBRA Elekta test (648 frames / 27 cases) and DeepFluoro test (104 frames / specimen 18-1109), so those two test sets are selection-biased for this detector and are listed under Tuning, not Testing.

Total.Criterion: Checkpoint selection (val list in data.yaml) for rx_lodo_carmlspine_1024: COBRA Elekta test (27 cases, 648 frames) and DeepFluoro test (specimen 18-1109, 104 frames).
Total.Comments: 27 COBRA patients plus one cadaver. Numbers scored on these two sets by this detector are not clean (or_ready/audit/AUDIT.md, Other observations); only its held-out-device numbers are.

Total.Criterion: Device held out entirely: absent from the detector's training frames, from the render poses and from the calibration terms.
Total.Comments: 28 C-ArmLSpine acquisitions plus one phantom. Patient count is not given because a C-ArmLSpine case is an acquisition, not provably a person.

Total.Demographic: Unknown. The C-ArmLSpine DICOMs carry no PatientAge, PatientSex or PatientID; the manuscript cannot state the age and sex of its intraoperative population.
Total.Criterion: C-ArmLSpine fixed test split, md5(case) % 10 in 8-9: 28 cases, 56 frames (28 AP + 28 lateral), 287 truth vertebrae, 56 truth sacra, 54 frames with an agreed level. Surgio-B51 C-arm.
Total.Comments: Patient count deliberately omitted: 149 released cases are 149 acquisitions on five acquisition dates; whether they are 149 people is unknowable on disk. The sacrum detector's result the manuscript and model card quote is scored here at confidence 0.74, whole-vertebra boxes: 231 of 287 vertebrae (80.5 %; 74.1-86.8) and 43 of 56 sacra (76.8 %; 64.3-89.3) (SchwingNet/results/a1.json). The body-box convention recompute is pending (G5). Collimated variants: 175 frames with three vertebrae in the field (566 truth), 287 with one (345 truth).

Total.Demographic: One resin hip phantom, 19 poses; not a person.
Total.Criterion: Geneva hip, Philips BV Pulsera image intensifier, all 116 frames test only (splits.json train 0 / val 0 / test 1). 37 truth vertebrae, 87 truth sacra.
Total.Comments: A completely unseen device for every detector; non-spine anatomy contributes device statistics, not level truth.

Total.Criterion: Per-fold mixed crop bank behind the level encoder and head (fold 0 shown; folds 1-4 differ only in the carm_* counts: 15,897 / 16,183 / 15,985 / 16,232 C-ArmLSpine crops and 123 / 120 / 112 / 124 C-ArmLSpine train+val cases). Split by case; 0 crops of the fold's 35 test cases; 0 split-rule violations (or_ready/audit/AUDIT.md, CV table).
Total.Comments: Image count is context crops, not films; one film or render yields several crops. Patient counts per fold bank are not recorded and are not additive across sources; corpus-level person counts are given per subset as upper bounds. The encoder was initialised from allspine_v2_r1, trained on a bank with the two split leaks listed under Noise (10); that leak does not touch the C-ArmLSpine test cases.

Total.Criterion: C-ArmLSpine crops (carm_AP 7,869 + carm_LAT 7,827) from the 113 train + val cases of fold 0.
Total.Comments: Persons unknown (acquisition-keyed).

Total.Sex: Not read for this card; the CSXA descriptor table carries it
Total.Criterion: CSXA cervical lateral radiographs with released per-vertebra levels; 4,963 films = 4,963 individuals by the descriptor (one-image-one-patient is untested).
Total.Comments: Patient count is the whole corpus; the number of films behind these 1,758 crops is not recorded.

Total.Criterion: BUU-LSPINE lateral radiographs (endplate lines L1-L5 + S1; levels assigned by position). 3,600 patients by the released table; possibly 3,598 (two byte-identical film pairs).
Total.Comments: Sex and age are encoded in BUU file names (<NNNN>-<F|M>-<age>Y) and are not aggregated here.

Total.Criterion: NHANES II lateral films with landmarks, entered twice: 236 films as nhanes (films_drr, 303 crops) and 208 as nhanes_drr (277 crops); 364 annotated sample persons across cervical and lumbar films. A digitised national survey film corpus, not a clinical one. The corpus holds 17,073 films of the 17,075 the CDC index lists; 543 carry landmarks and 16,530 do not.
Total.Comments: The two copies were split independently in the initialisation bank (Noise 10); in the fold banks both are training-side.

Total.Criterion: CT renders: ctsp_drr 638 (CTSpinoPelvic1K, 801 people in the corpus, release labels), verse_drr 940 (VerSe, 355 subjects), physics_drr 5,285 and physics_rare 1,132 (physics-styled renders of CTSpinoPelvic1K, VerSe and TotalSegmentator subjects; the rare subset is 81 transitional CTSpinoPelvic1K subjects).
Total.Comments: Persons: CTSpinoPelvic1K 801 (one TCIA PatientID per release id, verified two ways; 0533 truncated); VerSe 355; TotalSegmentator scans <= 1,935, persons unknown. Not additive: physics_drr renders the same people as ctsp_drr and verse_drr.

Total.Criterion: FluoroCap literature fluoroscopy panels, train only.
Total.Comments: Patient count: unknown and not reportable. Keying is by source document (about 1,197 documents, uncertain); one document can span several patients and one patient can appear in several documents; 72.8 % of panels are republished figures.

Total.Criterion: VinDr-SpineXR films in the capped encoder fine-tune bank (VINDRPS): 2,071 distinct released images, which contribute 2,632 crops. The release annotates lesions, not levels; levels were pseudo-labelled by fitting the run to a spine template and gated (tools/pseudolabel_real_films.py).
Total.Comments: Corpus 10,466 images / 5,000 studies. One number per object, each read from the object itself (grid jobs 40416442 and 40416535): 2,632 is a CROP count and was read as a film count until 2026-09-23; 744 films are the superseded lateral-only bank; 10,274 are pseudo-label files, 7,625 of which carry a named level and form vindrps_fov96_ctx (43,244 crops). The level bank the reported model was trained on (allspine_v8/v9) holds NO VinDr film. vindrps_fov96_ctx is keyed per image and its own validation leaks 77.8 % (Noise 11); no number from that bank is quoted.

Total.Demographic: Unknown (no age, sex or identity tag in the release).
Total.Criterion: C-ArmLSpine five-fold cross-validation test folds, md5(case) % 5 = k: 35 / 25 / 28 / 36 / 24 cases, every case tested exactly once; 148 AP + 148 lateral frames.
Total.Comments: Denominators in use, all from docs/carmlspine_cv5_mixed_2026-09-21.json and realxray/carmlspine/summary.json: 910 CBCT vertebrae compared by the two labellers -> 814 agreed; 1,807 projected truth boxes -> 1,623 with an agreed level; lateral complete coverage 676 agreed vertebrae in 143 cases -> 617 detector-matched in 141 cases (the 98.22 % denominator); AP 673 -> 631. Split by case; a person may in principle hold two acquisitions in two folds (see Partitioning scheme).

Total.Criterion: The 17 TotalSegmentator subjects on the validation (checkpoint-selection) side of every styled synthetic corpus (STYLE_INFO.json val_subjects: s0585, s0970, s1045, s1062, s1159, s1384, s1535, s1579, s1700, s1836, s1842, s1872, s1880, s1883, s1902, s2033, s2053); 1,998 validation entries in the P_pooled list. They select the styled-corpus arms' checkpoints, so no styled-corpus arm is held out on them.
Total.Comments: Used by the styled-corpus detector arms (dc_A, dc_B, dc_P), not by the model card's real-frame detector. These 17 subjects also appear in up to five CT render banks under other name forms (alias f), and the real-frame detector's render-trained parent (anchor_none_v2_17-1882) trained on renders of five of them (s0585, s0970, s1045, s1159, s1384) and validated on renders of one (s1062) (SchwingNet/results/eval_gate/EVALUATORS.md).

Total.Demographic: TotalSegmentator whole-spine subjects, mostly polytrauma CT (100 of 142); median age 60 years as released in meta.csv (v3.0.0 folder); ages are jittered by the release and one subject is recorded as 118 years and one as 0 years, taken as released.
Total.Criterion: Synthetic device corpus: 142 clean whole-spine subjects (~/model_night/ts_clean_subjects.txt) ray-cast under Cios Fusion, Elekta XVI and Surgio-B51 pose pools and styled through those devices' cards (five geometry x noise corpora: cios/cios 2,704 train, cios/surgio 2,704, cios/elekta 2,704, elekta/elekta 1,972, surgio/surgio 2,646).
Total.Comments: Feeds the styled-corpus detector arms only; the model card's detector is trained on real frames. Drawn with the clipped sampler (Noise 9). The datasheet names the source as TotalSegmentator v2 while the manifest path is the v3.0.0 release folder; the subject ids resolve in the v3.0.0 meta.csv (142 of 142).

Total.Criterion: Real frames used to fit each device's nine image-formation terms (tools/device_fit.py, six held-out folds, code SHA 6e1cf8d; fit.n_frames_fit per card): Cios Fusion 40 of 366 frames / six cadavers (held-out R2 0.905), Elekta XVI 40 of 335 frames (0.974), BV Pulsera 40 of 116 frames (0.952), PIXIUM 4600 14 of 18 frames / one cadaveric L1-L5 (0.679).
Total.Comments: R2 values are medians over folds; the gain over the uncalibrated baseline, mean over six folds with a bootstrap over folds (SchwingNet/results/a6.json), is BV Pulsera +0.042 [0.035, 0.053], Cios Fusion +0.015 [0.003, 0.027] (BCa [-0.0005, 0.027]), Elekta XVI +0.023 [0.005, 0.045], PIXIUM 4600 +0.070 [0.006, 0.131]; per-fold gains are negative on four folds (Cios -0.0128, Elekta -0.0010, PIXIUM -0.0412 and -0.0203); the plan's criterion holds on the percentile interval for all four devices and fails on the BCa interval for the Cios Fusion. The Cios Fusion frames are the same DeepFluoro frames listed above; they are not additional data.

Total.Criterion: Transitional test side of the built person-disjoint, subtype-stratified split (50/10/40 within each subtype; every real transitional subject on the test side): L6 43 CT persons + 3 real (C-ArmLSpine), T13 3 CT persons (tables/tab4_transitional.md; split_plan.md). These are the L6 and T13 rows only; all subtypes together hold 77 CT + 3 real test persons.
Total.Comments: No model of paper 1 scores these persons (SchwingNet/PAPER1_SCOPE.md); the three real C-ArmLSpine L6 appear in paper 1 only as cross-validation agreement with one labeller's read. The split-trained arm (encoder from ImageNet weights on the training side of the built person-disjoint split, because the v8/v9 level banks trained on 49 of the 54 L6 validation and test persons; docs/RESUME_2026-09-22_PM.md, checkpoint 2026-09-23 21:45; tables/tab4_transitional.md note d) is scored in paper 2 (SchwingNet/paper2_levelcheck/), whose manifest fixes bank, split, initialisation and recipe before unblinding; the manuscript shows only its development learning curve (supplement) and scores no held-out transitional person (SchwingNet/PAPER1_SCOPE.md). COBRA2026 screen calls (38 L6, 45 T13, 8 four-lumbar) are read by no person; a two-labeller count with both junctions in the field finds seven at-risk persons with an exported frame (Table 2, Figure 5c). How an unread test person enters paper 2's primary analysis is fixed in LEVELCHECK_MODEL.md (sections 4 and 14) and untouched by paper 1.

Partitions.Comments: Not scored in paper 1. Test side of paper 2's comparison against the frozen LevelCheck model (SchwingNet/paper2_levelcheck/).
